Bayesian calibration with a second predictor

Source: R/cal.ion.bayesian.R
cal.ion.bayesian.Rd

Fits a Bayesian regression of D47 on temperature and a second predictor (Ion) using Stan.

Usage

cal.ion.bayesian(
  calibrationData,
  IonError = NULL,
  numSavedSteps = 3000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 1L),
  MC = NULL
)

Arguments

calibrationData

The calibration dataset. It needs the columns Temperature (10^6/T^2, with T in K), TempError (1 SD of Temperature), D47, D47error (1 SD of D47), and Ion.

IonError

Ion measurement error (1 SD). Use a single value for all samples or one value per sample. Use NULL to treat Ion as known without error.

numSavedSteps

Total number of posterior draws to keep across all chains.

chains

Number of MCMC chains.

cores

Number of cores used to run the chains in parallel.

MC

Deprecated. Use cores instead.

Value

An object of class bayclump_cal with a single stanfit named BLM1_fit. Use cal.draws() to get the posterior draws.

Details

The model accounts for errors in Temperature and D47, and in Ion when IonError is given. Its sigma is the scatter left after removing the measurement error in D47. The true values of each predictor have a normal prior with a mean and SD estimated from the data. The intercept (alpha) and both slopes (beta and gamma) have flat priors. Both predictors are centered inside the model to improve sampling, and alpha is reported for Temperature = 0 and Ion = 0.

Examples

# \donttest{
ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S1", nobs = 50, seed = 1)
ds$Ion <- rnorm(nrow(ds))
fit <- cal.ion.bayesian(ds, IonError = 0.1, numSavedSteps = 1000)
#> Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)): error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'sampling': Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')
fit
#> Error: object 'fit' not found
